prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: refined desktop application logo for Pi App / Pith.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target: selected concept B, a custom white Greek π mark on saturated blue.
Primary request: make only these two design changes to concept B:
1. Make the central π very slightly taller / more vertically elongated, approximately 8% in its proportions. Preserve its distinctive sweeping upper bridge, left curved overhang, sturdy left leg, softly curled right foot, smooth rounded terminals, and pure-white color. It should still look like exactly the same crafted π identity. Scale the central π uniformly if needed to create space for the added brackets; do not make it skinny.
2. Add one pure-white left-facing code chevron "<" on its left, and one pure-white right-facing code chevron ">" on its right. The final emblem reads <π>. These are standalone code angle brackets, without arrow shafts. Match their softened corners and rounded ends to the central mark. Keep the π as the dominant element: each bracket is about 60–65% of the π height, and their stroke width is about 60–65% of the main π stems. Optically balance the bracket gaps, and align both brackets around the vertical center of the complete π. Make the whole <π> group feel like a single carefully designed software logo with generous surrounding blue, about 70% canvas width total.
Background: retain the original saturated royal-blue hue, but introduce a barely perceptible smooth blue-to-blue diagonal gradient, just slightly lighter at the upper left and slightly deeper at the lower right. Approximate endpoints #1B60FF and #1456F5. The difference should be subtle: at a glance the background should still read as solid blue. No obvious light spot, vignette, glow, grain, texture, banding, cyan, purple, or multicolor gradient.
Style: crisp vector-like flat artwork, white flat symbol, clean professional logo geometry, front view, square full-bleed opaque blue canvas.
Invariants: preserve concept B's π shape character and rounded drawing style. Change only the mild elongation, added code brackets, and extremely subtle blue background gradient. No words, caption, watermark, slash, extra icons, sparkles, borders, mockup, shadows, embossing, or 3D. Deliver one polished square logo image.
